extracted.subtask_description: Advice-oriented checklist for creating compelling fictional characters in stories and novels. Focuses on motivations, flaws, agency, arcs, and reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Character As Fulcrum
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters form the foundation; all story elements rest upon them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make characters the center of narrative decisions — plot, theme, and setting should pivot around them.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Cure For All That Ails
rubrics_metrics.description: A compelling character can compensate for weak plotting or themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize character interest; a strong character can carry scenes even when other elements falter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connected To Everything
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters are "the DNA in every goddamn cell" of the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure characters are woven into every part of the story so their presence influences tone, plot, and detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: You Are The Dealer; Character Is Drug
rubrics_metrics.description: Audiences become addicted to great characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft characters with hooks and addictive qualities that make readers keep coming back.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell Us What She Wants
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish clear objectives early; audiences must grasp motivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make characters' wants/needs explicit early so stakes and choices are understandable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not About Likability But Livability
rubrics_metrics.description: Audiences needn't like characters; they must want to spend time with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for characters who are interesting and inhabitable, even if they're not conventionally likable.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Give-A-Fuck Factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify upfront why audiences should care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signal stakes or emotional hooks early to secure reader investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rub Up Against Remarkability
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters must prove worthy of their own story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid blandness; give characters qualities, histories, conflicts or quirks that justify focus on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act Upon The World
rubrics_metrics.description: Proactive characters drive engagement; passivity creates dullness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor characters who make decisions and affect their environment rather than only react to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad Decisions Are Good Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Flawed, reactive choices create authenticity and tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow characters to err — mistakes generate conflict, growth opportunities, and realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: This Is Why Jesus Invented Suspense
rubrics_metrics.description: Beloved characters making poor choices create tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audience affection and characters' mistakes to heighten suspense and emotional payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: How You Succeed By Not Having Them Succeed
rubrics_metrics.description: Become an antagonistic force frustrating their path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce obstacles and frustrations that test characters and produce drama; failure can be narratively valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Each character maintains an internal moral compass; violations feel inauthentic unless earned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define each character's principles; if they break them, provide clear causes or arcs that make it believable.

rubrics_metrics.name: A B C
rubrics_metrics.description: Map three character transformations across your narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan incremental and substantive changes (three beats/turns) so the arc feels structured and earned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boom Goes The Dynamite
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide moments where audiences pump their fists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include satisfying high points — cathartic wins, revelations, or confrontations that reward investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware The Everyman, Fear The Chosen One
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid bland ordinariness and unearned specialness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make characters distinctive without relying on clichés like bland 'everyman' protagonists or deus-ex machina chosen-ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nobody Sees Themselves As Supporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary characters inhabit full lives where they're protagonists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat supporting characters as people with their own wants and perspectives, not just plot functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Main MC, DJ Protag
rubrics_metrics.description: Your protagonist should remain the most compelling presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the story anchored on a protagonist who maintains central interest, even amid a strong ensemble.

rubrics_metrics.name: You Are Not Your Character, Except When You Are
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't create self-inserts, yet infuse personal emotional experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid direct author stand-ins but draw on genuine emotion and experience to lend authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fugged Up
rubrics_metrics.description: Every character needs flaws and darkness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give characters moral, psychological, or behavioral imperfections to create depth and conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Tornado Beneath Cool Breeze
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance surface simplicity with underlying complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft characters who may seem straightforward on the surface but hide turbulent inner lives or histories.

rubrics_metrics.name: On The Subject Of Archetypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with familiar types, then transcend them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use archetypes as a starting shorthand but develop them beyond stereotype into unique individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue Over Description, Action Over Rumination
rubrics_metrics.description: Show character through speech and deeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer revealing moments in dialogue and action rather than long descriptive exposition or interior rumination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take The Test Drive
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiment with characters in informal writing first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try scenes, vignettes, or rough drafts to discover your character's voice and choices before committing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get All Up In Them Guts
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop intimate knowledge so choices feel inevitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know characters' backstories, fears, and desires deeply so their actions and arcs feel authentic and unavoidable.
